title: The Nest Club: clientele, decor and atmosphere
summary: He describes a mixed, high-class crowd of white and Black performers, the bandstand and decor, and bad man Bob Hewlett keeping order.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Uh hunh. Well, what about the Nest. What did it look like? Inside.
Well, the Nest was a nice little place. It wasn't too large and it wasn't too small. And it was a nice place for you to sleep in sometimes. When I got tired, I'd go in the back and go to sleep.

Well, we had some people in there. We had Otto Kahn. We had Henry Bussey, we had some -- Miller and Lyle. And Florence Mills used to come in there. Danny Small. We had so many. Bechet would come in there. Bechet was nobody then, but he'd come in there. And we had all the performers there like Glenn and Jenkins, and all. Black performers and white performers. I don't recall Paul Whiteman ever coming in there, but all of his men used to come in there. And quite a lot of Vincent Lopez' boys used to come in there.
So, in other words, the clientele there was not just white.
Oh, no, it was a mixture.
It was a mixture. As opposed to Baron's.
Yeah, it was different from Baron's -- Baron had -- and then this was a higher clientele than what Baron had. Baron had mostly the gangsters.
And beer barons, and all like that, see? But these were mostly per -- cause we had millionaires and everything coming up to the Nest, see. And they made a million dollars in one year.
Well, what, now was the bandstand raised? For instance, or --
Yeah, we was up about two feet, I guess.
Uh hunh. Describe it, what it looked like. The tables with tablecloths, or --

Well, oh they had tablecloths there and they had nice decorations, oh they went into this business right. We had a maitre d', and we had good waiters. No Trouble At All. If you started anything out -- very few people started anything because we had one of the legendary bad men up in New York at that time, Bob Hewlett, was always around there because Johnny Carey and Mal Frazier was his friends.
We had a lot of the girls there, what you would call then, 'call girls', at the time. You see, they were there, and both white and black. And Beautiful chorus girls. And when the
other shows would close, they'd all come into the Nest. The Nest was a sort of meeting place. And that was a darn good name for it because all the birds used to come flying in there.
